title: Score synthetic speech and listening tests
brief: Implement mel cepstral distortion with DTW alignment, F0 RMSE and voicing error, cosine speaker similarity, bootstrap intervals for MOS over raters and items, ASR word error rate, average ranks with SRCC and LCC at the system level, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
hints: mel_cepstral_distortion: slice [..., 1:] on both inputs to drop c0, then sum the squared difference over the last axis; the constant is 10 / np.log(10).
dtw_path: fill an (N + 1, M + 1) table D with D[0, 0] = 0 and infinity elsewhere, then backtrack from (N, M) by always stepping to the cheapest of the three predecessors until you reach (1, 1).
mcd_dtw: mel_cepstral_distortion(c_ref[:, None, :], c_syn[None, :, :]) is the whole (N, M) cost matrix in one call.
f0_rmse: both = (f0_ref > 0) & (f0_syn > 0) picks the frames to compare; (f0_ref > 0) != (f0_syn > 0) marks the voicing disagreements.
bootstrap_mos: np.percentile(replicates, [2.5, 97.5]) for level 0.95. Resampling whole raters and whole items is what keeps a harsh rater's scores together.

rank_with_ties: sort with np.argsort, then give every run of equal values the mean of the ranks it spans, (first + last) / 2 + 1 with 0-based positions. np.argsort(np.argsort(x)) gives ordinal ranks, which break ties by position.
lcc: center both arrays and compute sum(xc * yc) / sqrt(sum(xc**2) * sum(yc**2)). srcc is lcc applied to rank_with_ties of each input.
system_level: loop over np.unique(system_ids) and average scores[system_ids == s]; correlate those means, not the utterance scores.

wilcoxon_signed_rank: d = a - b, then d = d[d != 0] before ranking. W = rank_with_ties(np.abs(d))[d > 0].sum(). For the tie correction, np.unique(np.abs(d), return_counts=True) gives the group sizes t.
